summary: The J7 SHS is Chery's Jaecoo sub-brand undercutting the plug-in hybrid mid-size SUV class on equipment-per-dollar, and Australian reviewers are near-unanimous that the powertrain is the best part of the car: 90km of WLTP electric range from an 18.3kWh battery, a claimed 1200km combined range and an eight-year unlimited-kilometre warranty that carries no dealer-servicing condition. Where they disagree is the chassis — CarExpert and EV Central call the ride acceptable for the money, while CarsGuide, carsales and Chasing Cars mark it down for numb steering, loose body control and a fidgety, noisy ride on coarse Australian surfaces. Nobody rates it class-leading to drive, and the 340-litre boot, the missing braked tow rating and a service network of roughly 50 sites are the recurring practical objections.
pros: 90km of WLTP electric-only range from the 18.3kWh LFP battery — more than the BYD Sealion 6 Premium AWD's 81km and enough to cover a typical Melbourne commute on electricity alone

Eight-year/unlimited-kilometre warranty with no compulsory dealer-servicing condition, plus a separate eight-year unlimited-kilometre high-voltage battery warranty guaranteeing at least 70 per cent residual capacity — longer than BYD's 6-year and MG's 7-year cover
The petrol engine drives the front wheels directly in parallel mode as well as running as a generator in series mode, so highway efficiency does not collapse the way it does in a range-extender
40kW DC fast charging (30-80 per cent in about 20 minutes) is unusual at this price — the Sealion 6 and Outlander PHEV have no DC capability at all
Five-star ANCAP rating from 2025 testing, and both SHS grades sit far below the $80,809 ordinary LCT threshold so no luxury car tax applies
cons: 340-litre boot (to the cargo cover) is well down on the 424 litres of the front-drive petrol J7 and the 425 litres of a BYD Sealion 6 — the direct cost of packaging the battery — and the SHS is the only J7 with no spare wheel

Jaecoo quotes 5.9L/100km once the battery is depleted, not the 1.0L/100km combined label figure, and carsales measured about 6.0L/100km in charge-sustaining running with 8-9L/100km on the motorway, so the running-cost case largely evaporates for a buyer who cannot charge at home
No braked towing rating at all on the SHS (750kg unbraked only), where the petrol J7 is rated to 1350kg braked and a Sealion 6 Premium AWD tows 1300kg

Reviewers consistently criticise the steering as disconnected and artificial, the body control as loose when pushed and the ride as fidgety and noisy on coarse-chip roads, with abrupt regenerative braking and hesitant low-speed throttle response

Jaecoo launched in Australia in 2025 with about 50 service locations nationally and has already run repeated $3000 factory bonuses and cashback offers, so resale value is unproven and the transaction price keeps resetting
